subject: Physics
question: A stone is dropped from rest from the top of a cliff and hits the sea 3.0 s later. Calculate (a) its speed just before impact and (b) the height of the cliff. Ignore air resistance.
response_text:
Given $u = 0$, $t = 3.0\ \text{s}$, and taking $g = 9.8\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ downwards.

(a) Using $v = u + at$: $v = 0 + 9.8 \times 3.0 = 29.4\ \text{m s}^{-1} \approx 29\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

(b) Using $s = ut + \tfrac{1}{2}at^2$: $s = 0 + \tfrac{1}{2}(9.8)(3.0)^2 = 44.1\ \text{m} \approx 44\ \text{m}$.

The stone reaches about 29 m s⁻¹ after falling about 44 m. Because air resistance is ignored, both values are slight overestimates.

correct_steps: about 29 m s⁻¹ after falling about 44 m
